In detail

South Rotterdam, including Carnisse and Tarwewijk. Rotterdam runs a Veiligheidsindex as part of its Wijkprofiel, built from crime and nuisance figures together with a survey of around 30,000 residents between March and October 2025. Citywide it fell from 110 in 2022 to 104 in 2026, with the perception of safety dropping faster than the recorded figures. Both of those are council focus areas and both improved in the 2026 profile — but, unlike Hillesluis and Tussendijken, they improved by less than the council had targeted. Residential, with little visitor traffic.

Rotterdam publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does publish one, Wandroz uses it instead of an assessment. Where a review finds nothing documented, that is recorded as no findings rather than as a safety rating.

Frequently asked questions

Is Charlois safe?

Wandroz currently rates Charlois in Rotterdam as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Rotterdam during the day and roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Rotterdam at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Rotterdam publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Charlois safe at night?

At night, Charlois is rated as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Rotterdam. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Charlois a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Charlois's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Rotterdam) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. Is there official crime data for Charlois?

Not an official government crime feed — Charlois's rating comes from Wandroz's own current local/national press and survey research for this specific area instead (see the note on this page for what was checked and the sources used).
